name: Ghostwalk
one_liner: A browser-native 3D digital twin of a picking floor that replays ~2,000+ real orders (UCI Online Retail II, November 2011) through any slotting you build, then races a ghost picker on the old layout so every saved metre is measured on screen, not claimed — zero backend, zero API keys, zero cold start.
why_it_wins:
1) The pain is Indian and current: quick-commerce dark stores (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart) sell a 10-minute promise, so in-store pick time is the main controllable lever; in every fulfilment centre, travel is ~50% of a picker's time (Tompkins et al., Facilities Planning, 4th ed., 2010) and order picking is ~55% of warehouse operating cost (de Koster, Le-Duc & Roodbergen, EJOR 182(2):481-501, 2007). Where a product sits decides the walk; slotting is a free lever nobody can see. Ghostwalk makes it visible, interactive and scored.
2) The must-have IS the wow. For 4.2 the brief demands a 3D twin driven by real orders with before/after replay, so every hour spent on the visual is an hour on requirements; no other PS has this property. Other teams will show a three.js scene with a box moving; we show invoice IDs scrolling, a path that draws itself along aisles, a ghost picker racing the new layout, and counters diverging in real time.
3) The judge becomes the player. At 2:40 we hand over the trackpad: the judge drags one product, the monthly kilometres re-score in under a second (headless simulation, not the animation), and then our annealer beats the judge's layout live. "Mario Kart ghost for warehouses" is the sentence they repeat to each other afterwards.
4) It cannot fail on stage. Static site on Vercel (mirror on Cloudflare Pages, local vite preview on two laptops): no LLM rate limits, no Python cold start, no uploads, no tokens. Deterministic seeds shown on screen mean "replay" twice gives identical numbers.
5) Deep where it counts, explainable line by line: exact Held-Karp DP routing on an aisle graph (not Manhattan guesses), ABC baseline as required, simulated annealing with incremental delta evaluation as the AI opponent that exploits order affinity ABC ignores, and a chronological held-out split (1-15 Nov optimise, 16-30 Nov score) so the README reports in-sample and out-of-sample gains honestly. Every piece is 30-200 lines of TypeScript a human can walk through in Q&A.
6) Low competition, high reward: the judge-mindset scout rates 4.2 as the least picked (three.js scares ML students) with the highest ceiling. Against 30 teams of Streamlit dashboards and Gradio classifiers, a smooth 60-fps twin with real numbers is the one they remember.
demo_script:
Setup before the slot: app pre-loaded at https://ghostwalk.vercel.app (plus local `vite preview` on a second laptop, phone hotspot ready), browser at 125% zoom, Quality toggle verified on the demo laptop, OBS backup MP4 on both laptops. One narrator (N), one operator (O).

0:00-0:25 HOOK (slide 1-2, N talks over the 3D idle shot). "In a Blinkit dark store the promise is 10 minutes, and the picker spends about half the pick walking, not picking (Tompkins 2010). Where each product sits decides that walk. Ghostwalk is a digital twin that replays real orders through any layout and scores the walk before and after; the improvement is measured, never claimed."

0:25-0:55 DATA PROOF (M1). O opens the Data card: "UCI Online Retail II, November 2011: N invoices, N lines; cancellations removed: N; non-product codes removed: N (POST, D, M, DOT, BANK CHARGES...); top-100 SKUs cover X% of product lines; split 1-15 Nov optimise / 16-30 Nov held-out." O clicks a rack box in 3D: SKU card pops "85123A WHITE HANGING HEART T-LIGHT HOLDER, 1,2xx picks this month, slot C7". N: "Every box you see is a row in that JSON."

0:55-1:50 REPLAY (M2) — WOW MOMENT 1 "the self-drawing path". O presses Play. Camera (drei CameraControls.setLookAt, 1.2 s tween) swoops from the dock down aisle 3 and settles on a 3/4 isometric. HUD ticker: "Invoice 579xxx · United Kingdom · 7 lines". The picker walks the aisle graph; the cyan path draws itself ahead of him (drei Line with growing points slice, Bloom on); metres and seconds tick up (motion animate). Floor tiles under his feet warm from blue to red (heat memory). Speed stepper 1x -> 20x. Banner: "Animating 20 of N orders · monthly totals from headless simulate() in 0.4 s" and the month KPI tiles fill: "Original layout (random, seed 42): XX.X km · XX h · avg X.X min/order".

1:50-2:40 GAME (M3) — WOW MOMENT 2 "drag, and the month re-scores". O toggles Slotting mode: racks tint by pick frequency; fast movers are scattered (random original layout). O drags WHITE HANGING HEART from the far rack to bay A1 by the dock; the KPI delta flips to green ("-0.9 km this month") within 300 ms. O presses Auto-baseline (ABC: fast movers nearest the dock): the 3D boxes fly to their new slots (lerp), KPI shows "-NN%". N: "That is the baseline the brief asks us to beat."

2:40-3:10 JUDGE'S TURN. O hands a judge the trackpad: "Move any product. Try to beat ABC." Judge drags one or two; the counter updates live. N explains click-click swap works too.

3:10-3:50 THE GHOST RACE — WOW MOMENT 3. O presses Race the Ghost: the ghost picker (same mesh, 35% opacity, wireframe) walks the same orders on the OLD layout while the solid picker walks the NEW; two counters diverge side by side ("Ghost 18.4 km · You 12.9 km · -30%"); both leave heat trails; a 2D minimap mirrors the two paths so the projector audience can read it.

3:50-4:25 THE AI OPPONENT — WOW MOMENT 4. O presses Anneal (10 s budget, Web Worker): a progress curve draws live (iterations vs km, temperature readout, seed 42); boxes shuffle as the best-so-far improves; the Affinity overlay shows co-picked SKU pairs as glowing links pulled together. Leaderboard table lands with motion stagger: Original / ABC / Annealed / Judge, each on the optimise half AND the held-out half. N: "Held-out gain is smaller than in-sample; that is the honest number, and it is printed by the same `npm run eval` that produced the README."

4:25-4:50 STRETCH (only what is built and measured): Batch picking toggle (2 orders per trip, same simulate()) and 2-picker congestion (wait time counter); rack-visit heatmap; local leaderboard.

4:50-5:00 LIMITATIONS + LINKS (slide): UK gift retailer, not an Indian dark store (mechanics identical); top-100 subset with stated coverage; our layout, our speed/pick-time assumptions; synthetic original layout. QR codes: live app, repo. Q&A cards ready (see honesty_plan).
wow_visual:
Scene (React Three Fiber 9.8.2 + drei 10.7.9 + three 0.186.1, Vite 8):
- Warehouse: 6 aisles x 2 sides x 10 bays = 120 slots (100 SKUs + 20 empty), bay pitch 1.2 m, aisle width 2.5 m, rack depth 1.0 m (aisle pitch 4.5 m), front/back cross-aisles 3.0 m, packing dock at front-left. Floor ~30 x 20 m.
- Geometry budget: one InstancedMesh for rack frames (120 instances, 3 decorative shelf levels baked into one BufferGeometry), one InstancedMesh for SKU boxes (100 instances, per-instance `instanceColor` = pick-frequency heat or current selection), one InstancedMesh of floor tiles (60 x 40 = 2,400 instances, instanceColor accumulates visits = heat memory), one merged static mesh for walls/dock/labels, ContactShadows off, no shadow maps. Target <= 20 draw calls, <= 150k triangles, DPR capped at 1.5, `frameloop="demand"` when idle, "always" during replay.
- Picker: a capsule + head with bobbing animation (optional Kenney CC0 "Mini Characters" GLB swapped in if it loads under 1 MB); moves along the precomputed node path with constant speed lerp; the ghost picker is the same mesh with MeshStandardMaterial transparent opacity 0.35 + wireframe overlay.
- Path: drei `<Line>` (Line2) 3 px, cyan, `points` slice grows with the picker so the route draws itself; ghost path in amber dashed (`dashed dashSize 0.4`).
- Post-processing: @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1 `<Bloom luminanceThreshold={0.9} mipmapBlur />` + `<SMAA />`, `multisampling={0}`, Quality toggle (Off / Balanced / Cinematic) persisted in localStorage; default decided by a 2-second fps probe at load.
- Camera choreography: drei `<CameraControls>` (camera-controls 3.1.2) with scripted `setLookAt(px,py,pz,tx,ty,tz,true)` beats: dock reveal -> aisle fly-through -> 3/4 isometric; `fitToBox` on the selected rack; top-down ortho preset for Slotting mode.
- Game interaction: raycast on InstancedMesh (instanceId) for click-select and click-target swap (primary, trackpad/touch safe); drei `<DragControls>` for drag-to-slot with snap to nearest bay (enhancement); boxes animate to new slots with a 400 ms lerp; empty slots glow when a box is selected.
- HUD (React + Tailwind 4 + motion 14.5): order ticker (invoice, country, lines), metres/seconds counters via `animate(from,to)`, KPI tiles with diverging Ghost vs You numbers, SVG 2D minimap mirroring both paths, SA progress sparkline (SVG, ~100 points), Affinity overlay (drei LineSegments between top-50 co-picked pairs, width by count), Leaderboard with stagger reveal, Data card and Assumptions panel (speed, pick time, aisle geometry, seed).
- Projector readability: 20px+ HUD fonts, high-contrast dark theme, numbers in km with one decimal, minimap always visible.
wow_technical:
Core: one pure TypeScript `simulate(dataset, slotting, cfg, policy, subset)` used by scoring, animation, the baseline, the annealer and `npm run eval` — the animation only replays what the headless sim already scored.
1) Aisle graph + exact distances: grid graph (dock, front/back cross-aisle nodes per aisle, one node per bay inside each aisle; a bay node serves both rack sides). BFS/Dijkstra all-pairs over 121 nodes -> Float32Array of metres. Walking never crosses a rack by construction; the drawn path is the node sequence itself.
2) Per-order routing policy (switchable): Held-Karp DP O(k^2 2^k) for k <= 12 stops (exact tour dock -> stops -> dock), nearest-neighbour + 2-opt + Or-opt for k > 12 (flagged in output), and S-shape traversal (Hall 1993) as an ablation so judges see optimal vs heuristic routing on the same layout. Pick time = metres / 1.2 m/s + lines x 10 s (both parameters shown in UI).
3) Automatic baseline (brief requirement): ABC by pick-line frequency, SKUs assigned to the 100 slots nearest the dock in descending frequency (the 20 farthest slots stay empty).
4) AI opponent: simulated annealing over slottings. Neighbourhood = swap two SKUs or move a SKU to an empty slot; geometric cooling T_k = T0 * alpha^k (T0 set so 50% of random uphill moves are accepted at start, alpha chosen for a 10 s / 60 s budget); Metropolis acceptance; seeded PRNG (mulberry32, seed displayed). Incremental delta: inverted index SKU -> orders, cached per-order route cost; a move re-routes only orders containing the touched SKUs (~2 x avg SKU frequency), using NN+2-opt as the inner proxy and re-scoring the final layout with the exact policy. Runs in a Web Worker with progress messages; 60 s precomputed result committed as `data/layouts/sa_seed42.json` with its log, 10 s live run on stage. This captures order affinity (co-picked SKUs end up adjacent), which ABC cannot.
5) Honest evaluation: chronological split (orders 1-15 Nov = optimise set used by SA/ABC/player feedback; 16-30 Nov = held-out, scored only). Metrics printed by `npm run eval` into `eval/results.md` with commit hash: total walking distance (km) and avg pick time per order for Original (random seed 42, plus mean +- sd over seeds 1-10), ABC, SA, and any saved player layout, on both halves; routing ablation (optimal vs S-shape vs NN+2-opt) on the same layouts; SA convergence curve; lines-per-order distribution after top-100 filtering. Literature anchor for plausibility (not a claim): storage policy effects of 20-40% travel reduction in Petersen & Aase, IJPE 92(1):11-19, 2004.
6) Stretch computed by the same simulate(): batch picking (FIFO batches of B orders per trip, cart of capacity C lines, route over the union of stops), two pickers with aisle-segment occupancy (time-stepped; a picker entering an occupied segment in the opposite direction waits until it clears; wait seconds reported), rack-visit heatmap (visits Uint32Array exported from simulate).
What proves it: the leaderboard table on the held-out half, the routing ablation, the reproducibility of `npm run eval` (deterministic, no RNG outside the seeded annealer), and the on-stage re-score of the full month in <1 s after each judge move.
mvp_mapping:
M1 (pre-processing to JSON): `prep/prep.py` (Python 3.12, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0) reads the verified HF parquet mirror of Online Retail II, filters InvoiceDate to 2011-11-01..2011-11-30, drops Invoice starting with "C", drops exact duplicate rows (count reported), keeps StockCode matching ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$ with Quantity > 0 and Price > 0 (removes POST, D, M, S, DOT, BANK CHARGES, CRUK, AMAZONFEE, ADJUST, gift_*, C2, DCGS*), computes pick frequency = number of order lines per SKU, selects the top-100, builds the order list restricted to those SKUs (orders with >= 1 covered line), writes `public/data/orders_2011-11.json` {meta, skus[{code,desc,picks,qty}], orders[{inv,ts,country,lines[{code,qty}]}], split{opt,test}, affinity[[a,b,count]]} (< 1.5 MB gzipped) and `data/README.md` with every count. Satisfies "top ~100 products, how often each is picked, and the list of orders".
M2 (3D scene replaying orders): R3F scene with racks (instanced), 6 aisles, cross-aisles, packing dock, one animated picker that walks the aisle graph to each slot and back to the dock, path drawn along aisles only (BFS graph makes rack-crossing impossible), live metres and seconds counters driven by the same simulate() output, order ticker showing the invoice being replayed, speed control. Satisfies "racks, aisles, a packing dock and at least one animated picker... walks along aisles... live distance and time counters".
M3 (game mode with baseline): Slotting mode with click-click swap and drag-to-slot (snap), replay of exactly the same order list on the new layout, before/after KPI panel (km, hours, avg min/order) plus the Ghost Race animation, and the Auto-baseline button that applies ABC (fast movers nearest the dock) as the layout to beat; leaderboard rows Original / ABC / Annealed / Player on optimise and held-out halves. Satisfies "swaps or drags products between slots, replays the same orders, sees before/after walking distance and pick time... automatic baseline (fast movers nearest the dock)".
Order of work: M1 and the headless sim land first (hour 2), M2 by hour 4 (deployed walking skeleton for progress review), M3 by hour 8, stretch only after `npm run eval` reproduces every README number.
stretch_goals: Rack-visit heatmap: floor tiles and rack boxes coloured by visit counts from simulate() (instanceColor), toggle per layout, with a 'visits per slot' CSV export
Leaderboard of player layouts: name + km + layout hash in localStorage with JSON export/import; the README states it is per-browser (no backend) and lists the committed Annealed/ABC rows

Batch picking: one trip serves B orders (B = 2 or 3, FIFO by timestamp, cart capacity C lines), routed over the union of stops with the same Held-Karp/2-opt policy; KPI shows km and min/order vs single-order picking
Two pickers with congestion: alternate orders between picker A and B, time-stepped aisle-segment occupancy, opposite-direction entry waits; report total wait seconds and effective throughput
Simulated-annealing AI opponent with live progress curve and seed display (built as part of the core plan; counts as the originality item)
Affinity overlay: top-50 co-picked SKU pairs drawn as glowing links in 3D and listed in a side table, explaining why SA beats ABC
Routing-policy ablation toggle in the UI (optimal DP vs S-shape vs nearest-neighbour+2-opt) with the delta shown on the same layout
Dark-store preset: a second layout config (4 aisles x 8 bays, narrower aisles) to show the same engine on a quick-commerce footprint, clearly labelled as a layout change only
data_plan:
Dataset: Online Retail II, UCI Machine Learning Repository id 502, CC BY 4.0. Citation: Chen, D. (2019). Online Retail II [Dataset]. UCI ML Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CG6D. Columns: Invoice, StockCode, Description, Quantity, InvoiceDate, Price, Customer_ID, Country; 1,067,371 rows.
Acquisition (verified tonight by the data scout; UCI's own zip truncates from campus): primary `curl -L -o data/raw/online_retail_II.parquet "https://huggingface.co/datasets/vancevo/online-retail-ii/resolve/main/data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet"` (7.16 MB, PAR1 magic verified, 1,067,371 rows). Fallback 1: Kaggle anonymous `curl -L -A "Mozilla/5.0" -o data/raw/ori.zip "https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/mashlyn/online-retail-ii-uci"` (15.2 MB zip -> 94.85 MB CSV). Fallback 2: `https://huggingface.co/datasets/michaelmallari/online-retail-ii/resolve/main/online-retail-ii.xlsx` (45.6 MB, read with pandas engine="calamine"). The raw file stays out of git (.gitignore data/raw); `prep/download.sh` + `prep/prep.py` are committed and the processed JSON is committed.
Month: November 2011 (last full month; Dec 2011 ends on the 9th). Record the exact invoice and line counts in data/README.md; do not quote numbers before prep.py prints them.
Preprocessing (prep.py, deterministic): parse InvoiceDate; filter month; drop Invoice starting with "C" (count); drop exact duplicate rows (count); keep StockCode ~ ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$ (count removed, with the list of removed codes written to data/removed_codes.csv); keep Quantity > 0 and Price > 0 (count); pick frequency per SKU = number of order lines (not units; units also stored); top-100 by pick lines; orders = invoices with >= 1 top-100 line, keeping only covered lines (report lines-per-order histogram and the share of orders with >= 2 lines); coverage = covered lines / all product lines in the month and covered orders / all orders; affinity = co-occurrence counts of SKU pairs within invoices (top-200 pairs stored); split by InvoiceDate: 1-15 Nov -> `split.opt`, 16-30 Nov -> `split.test`.
Held-out protocol: ABC and SA are fitted on `split.opt` only (pick frequencies and SA objective computed on opt orders); the player's live feedback uses opt orders; every leaderboard row reports opt and test separately; the test half is never used to choose SA hyperparameters (fixed in advance: budget, T0 rule, alpha, seed 42).
Original layout: seeded random slotting (mulberry32 seed 42, displayed), with mean +- sd over seeds 1-10 in the README so "original" is not cherry-picked.
Attribution in README and in-app Data card: UCI id 502, CC BY 4.0, Chen 2019; HF mirror named as the download route; Kenney assets CC0 if used; figures quoted from Tompkins 2010, de Koster 2007, Petersen & Aase 2004 with full references.
architecture:
Fully static single-page app; all compute in the browser.
Components:
1) `prep/` (offline, Python 3.12): download.sh, prep.py -> `public/data/orders_2011-11.json` (+ data/README.md counts, removed_codes.csv). Run once, committed output.
2) `src/sim/` (pure TypeScript, no DOM): types.ts (Dataset, Order, Sku, LayoutConfig, Slotting = Record<code, slotId>), graph.ts (buildGraph(cfg) -> nodes/edges/slotNode[]/dockNode; allPairs() -> Float32Array metres), route.ts (routeOrder(stops, dist, policy) -> {order, metres}; heldKarp, nn2opt, sShape), simulate.ts (simulate(ds, slotting, cfg, policy, subset) -> {metres, seconds, perOrder: Float32Array, path per order (node ids), visits: Uint32Array}), slotting.ts (randomSlotting(seed), abcSlotting(opt), anneal(start, opts, onProgress) with inverted index + route cache), batch.ts and congestion.ts (stretch), rng.ts (mulberry32). Unit tests with vitest on a 2-aisle toy layout (hand-computed distances, DP vs brute force for k <= 6).
3) `src/worker/sim.worker.ts`: receives {cmd: 'score' | 'anneal' | 'abc'}, returns results and progress messages; the main thread never blocks.
4) `src/state/store.ts` (zustand 5): dataset, cfg, slotting, layouts {original, abc, sa, player}, replay cursor, KPIs, UI mode, quality setting.
5) `src/scene/` (R3F): Warehouse.tsx (instanced racks, boxes, floor tiles, dock), Picker.tsx (path follower, ghost variant), PathLine.tsx, CameraRig.tsx (CameraControls beats), Effects.tsx (Bloom/SMAA gated by quality), Affinity.tsx.
6) `src/ui/` (React 19 + Tailwind 4 + motion): HUD, DataCard, AssumptionsPanel, SlottingToolbar, KPIPanel, GhostRacePanel, AnnealPanel (sparkline), Leaderboard, Minimap (SVG), QualityToggle.
7) `scripts/eval.ts` (run with tsx via `npm run eval`): loads the JSON, runs every layout x policy x subset, prints a markdown table and writes `eval/results.md` with git commit hash and date; CI (GitHub Actions) runs vitest + eval on every push so README numbers are regenerated, never typed.
Data flow: JSON (fetch at load, ~1.5 MB gz) -> store -> worker scores Original/ABC/SA on load (<1 s) -> scene renders from store; a player move dispatches to the worker -> KPIs update -> scene lerps boxes; Replay/Ghost Race read the per-order paths already computed by simulate() and animate a subset at 1-20x.
Deployment: Vercel Hobby static (Vite build, `vercel.json` SPA rewrite), mirror on Cloudflare Pages (25 MiB/file limit is irrelevant), `.env.example` committed with a comment that no secrets are required; local fallback `npm run build && npm run preview` on two laptops. Repo layout per the judge-mindset checklist: README.md, DEV_LOG.md, .env.example, LICENSE (MIT), docs/architecture.md (Mermaid), docs/pitch/Ghostwalk_NexAI2026.pptx, docs/demo/script.md, data/README.md, eval/results.md.
stack: Node 22 LTS, TypeScript 5.9 (verify exact minor), pnpm or npm
@react-three/drei@10.7.9 (CameraControls via camera-controls@3.1.2, Line, Instances, DragControls, Html)
Python 3.12, pandas==3.0.6, pyarrow==26.0.0 (prep only; python-calamine only if the xlsx fallback is needed)

build_plan:
Wall clock: 22:00 IST 21 Oct -> 14:45 submit. Four coding agents on branches (feat/sim, feat/scene, feat/game, feat/opt-eval), humans integrate and own the demo; main receives a merge at least hourly (judge gate G1) with conventional messages; DEV_LOG updated every 2 h.
Agent A — Data + simulation core (first 4 h, then 2 h stretch sims): download.sh, prep.py and data/README.md counts (1 h); graph.ts + allPairs + vitest toy-layout tests (1 h); route.ts (Held-Karp <= 12, NN+2-opt+Or-opt, S-shape) with brute-force parity tests (1.5 h); simulate.ts returning totals, per-order paths and visits; sim.worker.ts; scripts/eval.ts writing eval/results.md (0.5 h). Later: batch.ts and congestion.ts (2 h). Deliverable contract: the function signatures in architecture; a 20-order fixture JSON so B and C can start before prep.py finishes.
Agent B — 3D scene (6 h): Warehouse.tsx instanced racks/boxes/floor from cfg (1.5 h); Picker.tsx path follower + ghost variant, PathLine growing slice (1.5 h); CameraRig beats + top-down preset (1 h); Effects + Quality toggle + fps probe, DPR cap, demand frameloop (1 h); raycast select/target swap on InstancedMesh, DragControls snap, box lerp (1 h). Perf gate: >= 45 fps at 1080p on an integrated-GPU laptop with Quality=Balanced.
Agent C — Game UI + state (5 h): store.ts + worker bridge (1 h); HUD, order ticker, KPI tiles, Minimap SVG (1.5 h); Slotting toolbar, Auto-baseline, Reset, Ghost Race panel with diverging counters (1.5 h); Data card, Assumptions panel, Leaderboard (localStorage) (1 h).
Agent D — Optimiser + evidence + docs (5 h): abcSlotting + randomSlotting with seed display (0.5 h); anneal() with inverted index, cached routes, incremental delta, progress messages; 60 s precomputed layouts committed under data/layouts/ (2 h); AnnealPanel sparkline + Affinity overlay data (1 h); README (12 required sections), DEV_LOG.md, docs/architecture.md Mermaid, .env.example, LICENSE, GitHub Action running vitest + eval (1.5 h).
Humans (continuous): 22:00 repo init + first commit (README skeleton, DEV_LOG noting 18:00-22:00 was planning, .env.example, .gitignore, LICENSE); 23:30 Vercel project linked so every merge deploys; 02:00 walking skeleton live (M1 + M2 basic, for any progress review); 06:00 M3 + ABC + SA merged; 09:00 polish, stretch gated by eval; 11:00 feature freeze tag; 11:00-12:30 `npm run eval` re-run, README/DEV_LOG final, numbers cross-checked app vs README vs deck; 12:30-13:30 record 5-min demo (OBS) + 3-min YouTube cut, generate .pptx via python-pptx from docs/pitch/deck.py; 13:30-14:15 LinkedIn + X posts with #NEXAI2026, clip, repo + live URLs; 14:15-14:45 smoke test on a different laptop and a phone, local preview fallback verified; 14:45 submit.
Integration/QA (humans + Agent A after hour 6, ~3 h total): merge order sim -> scene -> game -> opt; conflict surface is only store.ts and types.ts (frozen at hour 2); Q&A cards written by the humans from the code they merged (judge gate G10: each file has a named owner in README).
Estimated agent-hours: A 6, B 6, C 5, D 5, QA 3 = 25 agent-hours inside ~13 wall-clock hours of building plus 2 h of packaging.
risks: Laptop GPU stutter on the projector machine -> instancing only (<= 20 draw calls), no shadows, DPR cap 1.5, Quality toggle with fps probe, Bloom off by default on integrated GPUs; test on the actual demo laptop by 09:00 and keep a 'Minimal' preset
Drag-and-drop in 3D is fiddly on a trackpad -> click-select then click-target swap is the primary interaction; DragControls is an enhancement; a top-down ortho preset makes targets large

Simulated annealing too slow in the browser -> NN+2-opt proxy inside the loop, inverted index + per-order route cache, 10 s live budget with a committed 60 s result; final numbers always re-scored with the exact policy and the proxy is stated

Top-100 SKU coverage is modest (expected 20-30% of lines) and orders shrink to few lines -> coverage and lines-per-order histogram shown in the Data card and README; 'the twin models the forward-pick area'
Judge asks whether the score comes from the animation -> headless simulate() re-scores the whole month on stage in < 1 s; banner states 'animating 20 of N orders'

Judge asks 'where is the AI?' -> the annealer is a search-based optimiser that learns order affinity from data, exact DP routing, data-driven twin; honest answer that an LLM would be theatre for a combinatorial problem; the brief itself lists simulation and game design as the skills

Non-determinism or drifting numbers between app, README and deck -> single simulate() path, seeded PRNG, `npm run eval` in CI writes eval/results.md with commit hash; deck numbers copied from that file at freeze
Hourly commit rule broken overnight -> agents commit to branches every 30-45 min and a human merges to main hourly; a 45-min timer reminder; DEV_LOG timestamps
Data download fails on campus bandwidth -> HF parquet (7 MB) verified tonight; Kaggle anonymous and xlsx fallbacks scripted; raw file cached on two laptops immediately
Vercel build or outage during judging -> Cloudflare Pages mirror plus `vite preview` on two laptops and a phone hotspot; backup MP4 recorded by 13:30

R3F/drei/three version mismatch -> exact pins (three 0.186.1, fiber 9.8.2, drei 10.7.9, React 19.3.1, postprocessing peer three < 0.187 satisfied); lockfile committed at hour 1; never install the R3F 10 alpha
Held-Karp on a 20-line order blows up -> hard cutoff at 12 stops with NN+2-opt+Or-opt fallback, flagged per order in the eval output

Over-scoping stretch goals -> gate: no stretch branch merges before `npm run eval` reproduces every README number and M1-M3 are live; batch picking first (cheapest, measured), congestion second, dark-store preset last
honesty_plan:
Metrics: every number shown in the app, README and deck comes from `npm run eval` (scripts/eval.ts), which writes eval/results.md with the git commit hash, date and the exact table: layout (Original seed 42 with mean +- sd over seeds 1-10, ABC, Annealed, saved Player) x subset (optimise 1-15 Nov, held-out 16-30 Nov) x metric (total km, total hours, avg min/order), plus the routing ablation (optimal DP vs S-shape vs NN+2-opt) and the SA convergence log. CI re-runs it on every push, so a stale README fails loudly.
Held-out discipline: ABC frequencies and the SA objective use only the optimise half; SA hyperparameters (budget, T0 rule, alpha, seed) are fixed in DEV_LOG before the first run on the held-out half; the in-sample gain is expected to exceed the held-out gain and both are printed side by side with that sentence in the UI.
Data provenance (judge gate G5): in-app Data card and README list the source (UCI id 502, CC BY 4.0, Chen 2019), the download route, and every cleaning count (month rows, C-invoices removed, duplicates removed, non-product codes removed with the code list, rows with Quantity <= 0 or Price <= 0 removed, coverage of top-100 by lines and by orders, lines-per-order histogram). No scraped or private data; Kenney assets credited if used.
Declared assumptions (README + Assumptions panel): layout is ours (6 x 2 x 10 slots, 1.2 m bay pitch, 2.5 m aisles, 4.5 m aisle pitch, 3 m cross-aisles, dock position), walking speed 1.2 m/s, 10 s per pick line, single-order picking with return to dock in the base case, one SKU per slot, no cube/weight/replenishment, original layout is a seeded random slotting; the routing policy is the same for before and after.
Limitations stated on the last slide and in README: the dataset is a UK online gift retailer, not an Indian dark store (the slotting mechanics are identical; the framing is an analogy); only the top-100 SKUs are modelled with stated coverage; pick frequency counts order lines, not units; congestion and batching are modelled only in the stretch modes and do not change the headline numbers; the leaderboard is per-browser (no backend); the literature figures (Tompkins 2010, de Koster 2007, Petersen & Aase 2004) are context, not results.
Animation disclosure: the HUD banner says which orders are animated and that totals come from the headless simulation; a 'Replay whole month' button re-scores live so judges can press it twice and see identical numbers.
Watch-outs mapped to code: C-invoices and non-product codes removed in prep.py (counts shown); aisle-following distances via the BFS graph (path drawn on the floor so no rack is crossed); simple instanced geometry with a quality toggle for average laptops.
Process evidence: hourly commits, DEV_LOG with decisions, experiments (SA budget vs result, proxy vs exact), rejected ideas (LLM narration, Python backend, WebGPU), and the AI-tools declaration (Claude Code agents for scaffolding/tests/docs, every merged file reviewed and owned by a named team member who answers for it in Q&A).
Q&A cards (<= 20 s each): the split; the original layout; whether the score comes from the animation; why top-100 and the coverage; the speed and pick-time assumptions; why SA rather than an LLM; how it scales to 5,000 SKUs (same code, instancing, O(orders x route)); what congestion/batching change; which member built which module; what we would do with one more day (replenishment, cube, multi-level racks, real dark-store order data under NDA).
